scope: TLS termination check: a self-signed certificate, deploy/console-tls-proxy.ts terminating HTTPS in front of a stub upstream that serves the real built console page, HTTP to HTTPS redirection, the transport security headers, the proxy's handling of attacker supplied hosts and oversized bodies, and its own refusals. Not a public certificate, not a running installation, not the operator's chosen proxy (nginx, Caddy, the platform proxy).

checks.check: stub upstream serving the real built page
proxy announced its HTTPS port
proxy binds the HTTPS and the redirect port it was given
the built page is served over HTTPS unchanged
HTTPS carries the transport security header
HTTPS forbids content sniffing
an asset is served over HTTPS byte for byte
a management route is reachable through the proxy
the proxy tells the upstream the original protocol was https
a client supplied Host header cannot override the configured public host
plain HTTP is redirected to HTTPS
the redirect never points at a client supplied host
a declared body over the limit is answered 413 without being read
a body within the limit still reaches the upstream
a group or world readable key is refused
a non-loopback upstream is refused
a missing certificate argument is refused
a missing public host is refused
a public host that is not a bare host name is refused
the proxy shut down on SIGTERM
both ports are released after shutdown
